title: Design: MCP / AI Chat "script mode" on the existing cam JS engine (run / job / look) to cut agent cost and tool calls

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
@NeoTech, a design question for you. The idea and its measurements are @dudedagger42's: his SolidCraft script-mode work, carried over to CamCraft here. (mkinney is following this closely.)

**Prior art.** tangency-labs/solidcraft#12642 by @dudedagger42 added a "script mode" (scx) to SolidCraft's MCP server. The agent got three tools instead of dozens: `run` (a short script in a CAD vocabulary), `design` (state) and `look` (a view). Every `run` reply ended with a diff of what changed. Measured on SolidCraft's benchmarks: **59% less cost per task and 58% fewer tool calls at the same accuracy**, holding on Haiku, Sonnet and Opus. SolidCraft's maintainer closed it **only because it embedded a Python interpreter** ("will never ship a Python interpreter, sandboxed or not"), not because of the idea.

**Why CamCraft is in a better position.** CamCraft already ships a sandboxed JavaScript engine (boa) with the job-script API: the `cam` global, `assets/scripts/cam.d.ts`, VERBS in `crates/app/src/script/mod.rs`. There is no fs, no fetch and no console, and every side effect is a `cam` verb that rides the command history. A script mode would therefore need no new interpreter and no new host access.

**Proposal (to decide, not yet to build):**
- `run`: execute a short `cam` script as **one undo step**. The reply ends with a compact diff: tools and operations added or changed, op statuses, warnings, verify result. It refuses by name on the first failing verb, and rolls back the step.
- `job`: a compact document summary (not the full `get_job` JSON).
- `look`: a text or image view to check the work.
- The usual MCP tools stay for clients that want them. Script mode is an option of `camcraft-cli mcp` and of the in-app AI Chat.

**Why it matters now:**
- The reporter's measured AI Chat session cost about $0.45 per prompt, mostly from re-sent tool lists and large JSON results (#3784).
- Fewer round trips give faster replies.
- One script maps to one "Undo Turn".
- Local models handle 3 tools far better than about 150 (#3789's benchmark: small models fail most change tasks).

**Open questions:**
1. Does the `cam` verb set cover the common chat requests (add tool, add op with params, generate, verify, post, stock and WCS)? Which MCP tools lack a verb?
2. Is a diff reply enough to check the work, or does `look` need a render?
3. Do we keep both modes, and which is the default for AI Chat?
4. Safety: script verbs go through the same commands and refusals as the GUI. Confirm that no verb bypasses a check.

**Done means:** a decision comment here. If yes, a first measured slice: the 20-task local-model benchmark (`~/bench/local-models`) plus one cloud model, run with the current tools vs. script mode, reporting cost, calls and accuracy, followed by sub-issues for the build.

Related: #3784 (chat cost), #3789 (model recommendations), #3783 (providers).
